text:
maria: FYI saw a p99 tail spike after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. p95 stayed fine but p99 jumped ~2.5x. Suspect interaction with continuous-batching + kv cache churn.

ajay: rough numbers? which model/config? :thinking:

maria: running gptx-7b-v2 on prod-dedicated; baseline before change: p95=120ms p99=360ms RPS=1250. After change: p95=130ms p99=920ms RPS=1180.

sophia: that's huge. any correlation with max_wait_ms or max_batch_tokens changes?

maria: we did bump max_batch_tokens to 8192 in scheduler to allow denser batches (was 4096), left max_wait_ms at 8ms. Suspect larger batches + kernel fallback edges cause long tail when KV misses hit fallback kernels.

mark: can you dump the scheduler queue timestamps + kernel-choice tag for the p99 traces? we need to see if the slow ones are waiting or execution-bound.

maria: attached a quick tail sample (trimmed) — message format: [queue_wait_ms, exec_ms, kernel]
```
[12, 210, aten_kernel_v1]
[6, 80, fused_kernel_fastpath]
[10, 185, aten_kernel_v1]
[7, 75, fused_kernel_fastpath]
[15, 420, aten_kernel_v1]  # p99-ish
```

ajay: looks like two factors: >10ms queue wait for some requests AND aten_kernel_v1 is ~2x slower. Where is aten_kernel_v1 coming from? kernel selector fallback on long seqs / kv cache rebuild?

sophia: we instrumented kernel selection: selector picks fused_kernel_fastpath for short seqs and FP16-quant kernels for long sequences unless stateful KV cache invalidation forces aten fallback. KV miss rate spike?

perf-bot: auto-report: kv_cache_miss_rate increased from 2.1% -> 8.9% in the 5m window post-deploy; avg microbatch size +17%; median seq_len +9%.

maria: experiment plan: try lowering max_wait_ms from 8 -> 4 and reduce max_batch_tokens 8192 -> 6144 on a canary. hypoth: reduce queueing tail and force smaller microbatches so more requests hit fused_kernel_fastpath and cache hit locality improves.

mark: tradeoff note: expect throughput drop. quantify p95/p99 and RPS. if p99 improves but RPS drops too much we may need adaptive policy: low max_wait_ms for p99-sensitive routes, higher for throughput jobs.

ajay: also consider prewarming / warming hints to pin kernels for common seq lengths so we avoid kernel JIT/fallback latency. and maybe KV cache prefetch after a miss to avoid repeated misses in a short window.

maria: canary results (30m): config below. results after 30m: p95=135ms (up +5%), p99=230ms (down from 920ms), RPS=1089 (down -7.6%). kv_miss_rate -> 3.4%.
```
# scheduler config
max_batch_tokens: 6144
max_wait_ms: 4
microbatch_target: 48
```

sophia: that's promising — p99 improved massively with modest throughput loss. microbatch_target tweak probably reduced variance.

mark: next: run a 2h canary, capture kernel switch counts, and see if aten_kernel_v1 occurrences drop. if still present, add kernel affinity hints for common seq lengths. also check if quantized-kernel fallback path has cache-invalidations.

maria: noted. I'll roll the 2h canary and collect kernel-choice histogram + queue wait distribution. action items: 1) 2h canary (maria) 2) prototype kernel affinity hint (ajay) 3) KV prefetch prototype (sophia).

ajay: one more thought — add a short-term penalty in selector for kernels that have JIT time > threshold to avoid choosing them for latency-sensitive microbatches.

maria: agreed. will include selector-penalty metric in the next run. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled-dash-update: canary-metrics will appear under /dash/eng-runtime/canary/1787654321 in ~5m.
